title: Profiles and configurations
summary: A device profile says what a kind of device measures and accepts: its parameters. A device configuration says where one device's values come from: which announced metric feeds which parameter, and how it is converted. Drafts on both sides are editable; a published profile revision and an activated configuration snapshot are never changed.

boxes.label: Device profile
boxes.detail: The editable side. Any edit to a published profile turns it back into a draft and raises draft_revision, which every change must carry. Publishing never touches devices: each device stays on the revision its configuration names.

boxes.label: Parameters
boxes.detail: Each parameter has a UUID, a kind (state, measurement, counter, event or derived) and flags for reports_state and accepts_command. Once published, its key, kind and data type are fixed and its key is never given to another parameter, because devices, dashboards and history bind to it. Derived parameters are filled by calculations, not by a mapping.

boxes.label: Profile artifact
boxes.detail: Publishing validates the draft and compiles it into one canonical device-profile.v2 definition: parameters, calculations and alarm templates, with its hash. The definition is never edited afterwards. The next publication only changes the earlier artifact's status from active to retired, and devices on it keep working.

boxes.label: Discovered source
boxes.detail: What an edge node or device announced in its birth: metric names and datatypes. birth_revision goes up when that set changes. A source is reserved by at most one device.

boxes.label: Device draft
boxes.detail: Editable JSON on the device row, guarded by draft_revision. It names one artifact, one source with the birth revision the person reviewed, and the mappings. After the first activation the artifact must be a revision of the same profile, and the source cannot change while a configuration is applied.

boxes.label: Device configuration
boxes.detail: A device-configuration.v2 definition stored at activation with its hash. It embeds the artifact's canonical JSON and hash, the source and the resolved mappings, so it is complete on its own. The model refuses updates and deletes. A rollback copies an old snapshot into a new one with the source's current birth revision.

boxes.label: Mappings
boxes.detail: Every reported parameter that is not derived needs exactly one mapping to a metric whose datatype fits. A mapping can name a command metric when the parameter accepts commands. conversion_mode is profile, custom or none, and the resolved multiplier and offset are stored in the snapshot. Conversions apply only to read-only numeric measurements and counters.

boxes.label: Device row
boxes.detail: desired_configuration_uuid is the snapshot Laravel asked for; applied_configuration_uuid is the one the runtime confirmed; last_applied_configuration_uuid is what a resume uses. Commands are accepted only for the applied snapshot.

boxes.label: Runtime
boxes.detail: Receives the whole snapshot inside device.activate.v1 and needs nothing else: it parses the embedded profile, checks the mappings against the source's birth, then converts, validates and calculates each reading.

steps.text: A profile's parameters, calculations and alarm templates are edited as a draft. Published parameters keep their key, kind and data type.
Publishing compiles the draft into an artifact: one canonical definition with a hash. The previous artifact is retired but stays usable.
A device's draft picks one published revision. Publishing a newer one changes nothing for the device until someone activates it.
The draft also picks a discovered source and maps its announced metrics to the profile's parameters.
Activation compiles the draft. It fails if a reported parameter is unmapped, a datatype does not fit or the source has a newer birth than the one reviewed.
The snapshot stores each mapping with its resolved conversion, so a later change to the profile's default conversion does not reach this device.
The device points at the snapshot as desired, and as applied once the runtime confirms it. Earlier snapshots stay as history for rollback.
The runtime gets the complete snapshot, profile included, and maps the source's metrics to readings with it.
